title: Deadly Diseases and the Theory of Evolution
author: Alan Gillen
target_audience: Christian readers interested in science and origins
Educators and students in Christian schools or homeschool contexts
Laypeople seeking to understand disease from a biblical perspective
Readers critical of mainstream evolution theory
core_themes: Origins of disease in a biblical context
Critique of evolutionary theory regarding disease development
Role of mutation, adaptation, and natural selection
Biblical creation vs. naturalistic explanations for disease
Medical and biological evidence for design
primary_purpose: To examine the origin and development of infectious diseases through a biblical creationist lens, challenging evolutionary explanations and highlighting examples that support intelligent design and the biblical account of origins.

structure_format.narrative_style: Expository, accessible, and argument-based with biblical integration
structure_format.organization: Thematic chapters addressing disease mechanisms, historical outbreaks, and evolutionary arguments
features: Case studies of historical epidemics (e.g., bubonic plague, smallpox, Ebola)
Discussion of microbiology and genetics in a creationist framework
Scripture references tying findings to biblical text

key_concepts_lessons: Diseases are not evidence of molecules-to-man evolution but often a result of deterioration, loss of information, or adaptation within a biblical worldview.
Pathogens frequently exhibit adaptation and microevolution, but not the upward complexity predicted by macroevolution.
The emergence and spread of disease fits within the Genesis account of a fallen world suffering from the consequences of sin.
Mutations generally reduce or modify function rather than create new complexity.
Medical and microbiological evidence can be interpreted as supporting the original 'good' creation, later marred by corruption and decay.
notable_features: Detailed discussion of famous diseases and their histories
Integration of scriptural analysis with scientific content
Charts and illustrations explaining microbial adaptation
Sidebars on key terms and concepts
Sections addressing common questions on disease and creation
cultural_historical_context: Published in the 2000s amid ongoing debates between evolution and creationism, especially in the United States; reflects increasing interest within evangelical circles to provide faith-based alternatives to mainstream scientific narratives.
reception_impact: Appreciated by the creationist/Christian homeschooling community for accessible explanations
Recommended by ministries and organizations promoting biblical creationism
Criticized by mainstream scientists and educators for opposing consensus evolutionary science
Used in Christian education settings as a supplemental resource
comparable_titles: The Genesis of Germs by Alan Gillen
The Lie: Evolution by Ken Ham
Icons of Evolution by Jonathan Wells
